contexts.title: Virtual loop logistics
contexts.text:
INTERVIEW DAY LOGISTICS - virtual loop
Date: Tuesday, October 7. All times Mountain.

09:00 - 09:15  Welcome with recruiting coordinator Sunniva Pratt
09:15 - 10:15  Ledger design exercise (a shared whiteboard link arrives 10 minutes before)
10:30 - 11:30  Go coding session (use your own editor; screen share required)
11:30 - 12:15  Break
12:15 - 13:00  Values conversation with Imani Castellanos

Tech check: join the video link 5 minutes early and confirm your camera and microphone. If audio fails, dial the backup bridge at (555) 010-3321, PIN 4471 9022, and message Sunniva.
Reimbursement: none needed for virtual loops.
Accessibility: reply to Sunniva if you would like extra time, live captions, or additional breaks. We are happy to adjust.
Recording: sessions are not recorded.
After the loop: decisions usually arrive within one week. Please do not contact interviewers directly; route any questions through Sunniva so nobody gets left out of the loop.

items.speaker: other
items.question: Let's dig into Dockhand. How did the outbox part actually work end to end, what happens if the service dies right after the database commit but before anything hits Kafka, and how did consumers deal with duplicates?
items.expected_answer_type: first-person mechanism walkthrough without invented implementation specifics

items.speaker: other
items.question: The team you'd join has a couple of mid-level engineers who'd kind of look to you. Have you mentored people before? What did that look like?
items.expected_answer_type: first-person answer that does not invent mentoring history

items.speaker: other
items.question: Quick Postgres one. Under read committed, what are you actually protected from, and what can still bite you?
items.expected_answer_type: concise technical explanation of isolation guarantees and anomalies

items.speaker: other
items.question: If you build a binary heap bottom up from an unsorted array, what's the time complexity? And why isn't it n log n?
items.expected_answer_type: complexity result with a short correct justification

items.speaker: other
items.question: Tell me about Lanternfish. How did you actually land on that DNS number?
items.expected_answer_type: first-person technical walkthrough grounded in the resume

items.speaker: other
items.question: So you were primary on call at your last full-time job. Walk me through an incident you actually ran, like from the page all the way to the postmortem.
items.expected_answer_type: first-person incident answer without a fabricated incident

items.speaker: other
items.question: Okay, coding. Given a list of intervals, like one to three, two to six, eight to ten, merge the overlapping ones and return the result. Talk me through the edge cases, and give me time and space complexity when you're done.
items.expected_answer_type: working code with edge cases and complexity

items.speaker: other
items.question: This is supposed to give you a fresh list with just the new tag each call, but the list keeps growing between calls. def add_tag(tag, tags=[]): tags.append(tag); return tags. What's going on, and how would you fix it?
